title: Claim support, citations and evidence provenance
outcome: Separate claim truth, citation support, evidence coverage and source availability using an auditable claim-document relation.

exercises.title: One supported claim
exercises.task: Cite only c1 correctly among three eligible claims.
exercises.hint: The link and claim denominators differ.
exercises.answer: Perfect precision does not imply that the full answer has adequate evidence coverage.

exercises.title: No citations
exercises.task: Evaluate an answer with one eligible claim and no links.
exercises.hint: Distinguish an empty link denominator from absent claim support.
exercises.answer: There are no links to judge, but no eligible claim has supported evidence.

exercises.title: Unknown support relation
exercises.task: Add a link with no adjudicated support label.
exercises.hint: An unjudged pair is not a negative or positive label.
exercises.answer: Retain missingness and acquire a label or use an explicit assessment-sampling protocol.

exercises.title: Duplicate a citation
exercises.answer: Duplicated markup should not increase the apparent amount of evidence.

exercises.title: Use a newer document
exercises.task: Evaluate a day 10 answer with a day 12 document.
exercises.expected: That version is ineligible for the historical reconstruction.
exercises.hint: Use availability time as well as content.
exercises.answer: A later correction cannot be treated as information the original system had at decision time.

exercises.title: Disentangle truth and support
exercises.task: Construct a claim that accurately quotes an erroneous source.
exercises.expected: Support can be true while truth is false.
exercises.hint: Audit source authority and the task ground truth separately.
exercises.answer: Citation evaluation measures a relation to supplied evidence. It does not establish that all evidence is correct or current.
